chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Isḥaq ibn 'Ammar from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who is an old elder or a sick person who fears the crowding and pressing of people; he enters the state of Ihram for Hajj and departs to Mina before the Day of Tarwiyah. He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'So does a healthy man depart seeking a place or taking it easy with that?' He said: 'No.' I said: 'Does he hasten by one day?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'By two days?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'By three?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'More than that?' He said: 'No.'

key_terms.يَتَرَوَّحُ: to take it easy or settle comfortably
key_terms.يَوْمِ التَّرْوِيَةِ: the Day of Tarwiyah (8th of Dhul-Hijjah)
key_terms.يُحْرِمُ بِالْحَجِّ: enters the state of Ihram for Hajj

ai.seo_question: How many days early can elderly or sick pilgrims depart for Mina to avoid crowds?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexibility of the Mina residency rule, permitting the elderly and sick to depart one to three days before the Day of Tarwiyah to avoid the physical strain of the crowd (*zihām*), while healthy individuals are restricted to a single day's early departure. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of *raf' al-haraj* (removal of hardship), balancing ritual precision with practical ease for those with valid excuses.
